title: Kody’s Story: Staying Curious and Defending What’s Next
body_markdown:
Kody was in fourth grade when his family first got the internet. At the bottom of a web page, he spotted a link: build your own website for free. Most fourth graders were worried about spelling tests. Kody, with no coding experience and no idea where to start, was teaching himself web design.


Then, he built a site for himself.


Today, Kody Salsman is Nelnet’s Director of Cybersecurity, Protective Operations and Cyber AI. He leads the teams that use threat intelligence and hands-on testing to find and fix weaknesses in Nelnet’s systems before anyone with bad intentions can use them.


He jokes that he’s a defender of digital castles. “I’ve said that tongue in cheek, but as time goes on, it’s proven more accurate than I originally intended.”


# From Curious Kid to Cyber Leader


After earning a degree in information systems management at Doane University, Kody worked his way from an IT help desk role into cyber security, teaching himself about IT, information systems, and information security through webinars, trainings, and books. Before Nelnet, one of his first jobs in security was at a local bank, where he found himself building security operations from the ground up.


> I've probably been doing cybersecurity longer than enterprise cybersecurity has really even been a term.


**Kody Salsman**


Director of Cybersecurity, Protective Operations and Cyber AI


In 2020, during the pandemic, Nelnet gave him the chance to put that experience to work in a major way. He accepted a position as Security Operations Center Manager. In the six years since, he has led the Security Operations Center, run the vulnerability operations team, and now directs cybersecurity, protective operations and cyber AI.


Along the way, Nelnet’s investments in professional development and learning has helped Kody stay on top of the latest developments in cybersecurity, a field that changes as fast as the threats do.


# The Hackers on Our Side


Nelnet’s cyber defense runs on three colors.


Red plays the attacker, blue plays the defender, and purple is what happens when the two work together. Each team tests and learns from the others.


The red team is made up of associates who emulate what a real adversary would do and look for ways a bad actor could exploit Nelnet.


The blue team defends. It includes the Security Operations Center and the cyber threat intelligence team, which studies who is out there, how they operate, and what they are after, so the other teams know what to look for.


The two teams come together for “purple teaming”, where the red team carries out an attack, and the blue team tries to spot it. Each round sharpens Nelnet’s monitoring.


At the same time, a cyber AI team studies the new frontier. Can AI be exploited? Can it be made to do things it shouldn’t? Can it leak data? The team evaluates new models and builds with AI, too.


Kody’s multiple teams now share a home. Nelnet’s new Cyber Fusion Center in Lincoln includes a secure Security Operations Center with dashboards, a locked forensics room, and open space for collaboration. The “fusion” in the name is about bringing teams together. “In the event of something happening, we might have to get minds together,” Kody says.


# Defending at Machine Speed


Looking ahead, Kody sees the biggest change in how fast everything moves. In recent months, frontier AI models have become far better at finding vulnerabilities in code. Flaws that went unnoticed for years are now being found at a pace the industry has never seen.


The time to respond is shrinking. A vulnerability once gave attackers weeks to figure out how to exploit it, then days. Now, Kody says, attacks can begin before a flaw is publicly announced.


> You no longer have time to sit and wait to patch. How we do cyber defense is getting flipped on its head.


**Kody Salsman**


Director of Cybersecurity, Protective Operations and Cyber AI


That is shaping the conversations inside his teams. How can Nelnet move at machine speed? How can it add AI-powered defenses? Within a few years, Kody expects AI to be defending Nelnet right alongside his team.


For Nelnet, that raises the value of what the Cyber Fusion Center was built to do: red, blue, and AI teams learning from each other so the company can adapt as quickly as the threats do. A defender of digital castles, it turns out, doesn’t guard them alone.
